'''Howard Alan Masur''' is an [[Americans|American]] [[mathematician]] who works on [[topology]], [[geometry]], and [[combinatorial group theory]].<ref>[http://math.uchicago.edu/~masur/ Howard Masur at the University of Chicago]</ref><ref>[http://math.uchicago.edu/~chicagotopology/ First Chicago Summer School in Geometry and Topology]</ref>

== Biography ==
Masur was an invited speaker at the 1994 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Zürich]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByCongress.php |title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers since 1897 |access-date=2015-06-12 |archive-date=2017-11-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171108012153/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByCongress.php |url-status=dead }}</ref> and is a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society]</ref>

Along with [[Yair Minsky]], Masur is one of the pioneers of the study of [[curve complex]] geometry.<ref>{{cite book|author=Benson Farb|author-link=Benson Farb|title=Problems on Mapping Class Groups and Related Topics|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uiqDbaQRr7IC&pg=PA140|year=2006|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|isbn=978-0-8218-3838-9|page=140}}</ref> He also contributed to the understanding of the convergence of geodesic rays in [[Teichmüller theory]].<ref>{{cite book|author=Athanase Papadopoulos|title=Handbook of Teichmüller Theory|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PSL1SDKRtPcC&pg=PA115|year=2007|publisher=[[European Mathematical Society]]|isbn=978-3-03719-029-6|page=115}}</ref>

Masur was a Ph.D. student of [[Albert Marden]] at the [[University of Minnesota-Minneapolis]].<ref>[http://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=2458 Mathematics Genealogy Project]</ref>

== Awards and recognitions ==
The [[Hubbard–Masur theorem]] is named after Masur and [[John H. Hubbard]].<ref>R. A. Wentworth, "[https://www.math.umd.edu/~raw/papers/gardiner.pdf Energy of Harmonic Maps and Gardiner’s Formula]"</ref> In 2009, a conference of mathematicians honored Masur's 60th birthday in [[France]].<ref>{{Cite web|title="Dynamics and Geometry of Teichmuller Space (honoring the 60th birthday of Howard Masur). Luminy, France. June 18-20, 2009."|url=http://www.cpt.univ-mrs.fr/~masur60/|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923210903/http://www.cpt.univ-mrs.fr/~masur60/|archive-date=2015-09-23|access-date=2015-06-12}}</ref>
